analysis.title: Democratic Sweep Likely / QRA Ahead / ECB's Nagel / NZ Jobs
key_insights: Betting markets raised the probability of a Democratic blue wave from the mid-to-low 80s to above 98% during the Asia morning. NDX futures fell 1.3%, UST yields fell 6bp and the US dollar fell 40bp. Equities later pared losses and USTs gave back some gains.
Gold held up through the move and broke above 4,000, despite its recent correlation with equity corrections.

UBS Evidence Lab puts the implied probability of Democratic control at 97% in the House and 81% in the Senate. RealClearPolitics rates 47 Senate seats safe Democratic, 44 safe Republican and nine toss-ups, so the Senate may be tighter than betting markets imply.

The S&P 500 is up roughly 10% on a price basis through Nov. 2, against a typical 1.6% gain by Election Day in a midterm year. Bloomberg data show 2026 is the sixth-best start to a midterm year since 1950.

Panelists at the UBS APAC Hedge Fund Leaders Conference said opposition to AI data-centre development is increasingly bipartisan. Concerns include land, electricity and water use, local control, corporate concentration and job displacement. Texas and Pennsylvania are the key states to watch for gubernatorial restrictions.

Treasury's quarterly refunding borrowing estimates were $12bn above UBS Rates Strategy forecasts, or $38bn below after adjusting for cash-balance assumptions. UBS expects coupon auction sizes unchanged this quarter and a change in forward guidance removing 'at least'. The first auction size adjustments are expected in May 2027. Unchanged sizes could steepen the 10s/30s curve.

Bundesbank President Nagel said a December ECB rate hike is 'very likely necessary' unless the inflation outlook improves significantly. He said inflation is approaching the ECB's adverse scenario and price pressures are likely to run above the September projections.
BoC Governor Macklem said further rate increases may be necessary after the 25bp hike to 2.5%. Inflation is projected at or above 3% through much of 2027, returning near 2% by mid-2028.

New Zealand Q3 employment fell 0.1% q/q and the unemployment rate rose to 5.7%, the highest since 2015. UBS still expects 25bp RBNZ hikes in December (to 3.00%) and February, with a risk the December hike slips to February.

UBS Australia Economics expects the RBA to hold at 4.85% for a sustained period after three board members voted against a hike and the RBA dropped its tightening bias. Markets price cuts from March, which UBS considers too early. Any further hike is more likely in February 2027.
Moscow plans to seek further easing of US sanctions after the midterms, per Bloomberg. UBS expects no speedy resolution of the Ukraine-Russia conflict regardless of the midterm outcome.
China's RatingDog services PMI fell to 50.8 in October from 51.6. Input cost inflation hit a five-month high and selling prices were cut for a second month, which risks squeezing margins.
Turkey's core inflation fell 40bp to 28.3% y/y in October while headline rose to 29.8%. UBS expects a 100bp CBRT cut to 35% in December.
UBS holds a long EURUSD position, which has traded above 1.12 since entry, and exited the short USDCAD position around 1.40. The desk sees USD shorts staying in play.
AMD rose 8.5% after a Q3 beat and a Q4 revenue outlook of $17bn plus or minus 3% versus $16.3bn expected. Data Center strength was the standout and Client missed.
UBS analyst David Vogt sees downside risk for Apple from a Services slowdown and margin pressure. Services growth was around 10% y/y and the December guide is 8-9% versus UBS at 11.5%.

UBS prime brokerage data show equity long/short funds de-grossed -0.8std of US equities and -2.6std of EU equities on Monday. The US and Europe equity long/short deleveraging indicators triggered, and the desk expects further deleveraging.
The Nikkei 225 fell 3.6% to 60,835 and the Topix fell 2.5% to 3,833 as the Trump/AI trade unwound. Semiconductor and component names led the selloff while desk flows were 62% better to buy.
USDCNH rallied on a higher-than-modelled fix of 6.7180. USDCNH is now in the 6.6800/6.7000 resistance area.
USDKRW fell from 1347 toward 1336 on USD weakness, AI weakness and equity-related de-hedging. Equity outflows total about $2bn. Next downside levels are 1328 and 1318.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose 8.5%, in line with the ~8.6% implied move, after a Q3 beat and Q4 revenue guide above expectations, led by Data Center strength.

UBS analyst David Vogt flags a Services slowdown (December guide of 8-9% vs UBS 11.5%) and margin pressure from tariff roll-off, memory costs and constrained 3nm capacity, which could pressure the premium multiple.

earnings_insights: AMD Q3 reported 11/3 revenue $13.38bn versus $13.1bn expected. EPS was $2.09 versus $1.95 expected (basis not stated in the report).
AMD Q3 Data Center revenue was $8.55bn versus $8.25bn expected. Client revenue was $2.92bn versus $3.08bn expected. Embedded revenue was $1.11bn versus $1.08bn expected.
AMD Q3 gross margin was 55.9% versus 56% expected. Opex was $3.56bn versus $3.66bn estimate. Capex was $648mn versus $861.3mn expected. Free cash flow was $554mn versus $793mn expected.
AMD guided Q4 revenue to $17bn plus or minus 3% versus $16.3bn expected, with gross margin around 55% versus 55.3% expected.

Apple reported a quarter with better revenue on a strong iPhone print. Services grew around 10% y/y. Apple guided December Services growth to roughly 8-9% versus UBS estimate of 11.5%. UBS expects FY27 revenue growth of roughly 10-11% on broadly flat iPhone units and higher ASPs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Highest since 2015 and well above expected. It supports a slower pace of RBNZ hikes, though UBS still expects hikes in December and February.
Well below expected, reversing some of Q2's progress.
UBS expects 25bp hikes in December and February because inflation remains too high.
Likely to top 4%, which keeps the case for hikes.
Raised 25bp as high oil prices worsened the inflation outlook. Macklem said further increases may be necessary.
UBS expects a sustained hold. Any further hike is more likely in February 2027.
Slowest expansion since July, with input inflation at a five-month high and falling selling prices squeezing margins.
Down 40bp, supporting the CBRT easing narrative.
Ticked up slightly, though core and services inflation declined.
UBS expects the cut, in line with forward guidance.

risk_factors: Greater friction around AI and data-centre investment, the debt ceiling, fiscal policy and shutdown odds under a Democratic sweep.
Senate control may be tighter than betting markets imply, with nine toss-ups per RealClearPolitics.
Treasury holding auction sizes unchanged could steepen the 10s/30s curve and cheapen long-end spreads.
Further deleveraging in consensus trades such as hyperscalers and semis.
Oil price resurgence feeding inflation and further central bank tightening.
Geopolitical shocks could pause the CBRT easing path.
RBNZ December hike could be delayed to February after the Q4 CPI release.
Apple Services deceleration, tariff benefit roll-off, rising memory costs and constrained 3nm capacity.
vol_and_positioning: UBS prime brokerage data show equity long/short funds de-grossed -0.8std of US equities and -2.6std of EU equities on Monday, with continued pain in consensus trades (hyperscalers, semis). The US and Europe equity long/short indicators triggered and the desk expects further deleveraging.
In Asia, derivatives showed selective upside demand in Korea and Japan, but investors preferred low-premium structures, signalling limited conviction.
Borrow demand rose in selected AI, oil and Chinese optical names, and China index hedging costs remained elevated.
Front-end NZD option supply emerged, with 1w1m NZD and 1w1m AUDNZD looking stretched. The desk sees NZD risk reversals becoming better bid for puts.
USDCNH 1m basis traded at 430/410bp below zero given positioning.
geopolitical: US midterms: a Democratic sweep of Congress looks likely, per NBC News and betting markets.
Moscow plans to seek further easing of US sanctions after the midterms, per Bloomberg, including diesel, fertilisers, gas and frozen Russian assets.
The Kremlin has lost confidence in Trump's ability to pressure Ukraine into a settlement on Russian terms, per Bloomberg.
UBS hosts a discussion on Iran tensions and the Middle East outlook with Suzanne Maloney.
New Zealand election on Nov. 7: the desk sees a Labour win potentially restoring an employment objective to the RBNZ mandate.

tension_points.bull_case: Panelists at the UBS APAC Hedge Fund Leaders Conference argued opposition to AI data-centre development is increasingly bipartisan, so a Democratic sweep is not a uniquely larger risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets sold tech on the Democratic sweep repricing, with NDX futures down 1.3%, on a view of more friction around AI and data-centre investment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gubernatorial policy shifts or development restrictions in Texas and Pennsylvania would confirm the policy risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Unchanged auction sizes with guidance removing 'at least' signals future cuts, with the first adjustment in May 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Keeping auction sizes unchanged could pressure the 10s/30s curve steeper and long-end spreads cheaper.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Treasury announcing immediate long-end auction size cuts would contradict UBS's unchanged-sizes call.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price rate cuts from as soon as March after the RBA dropped its tightening bias.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS says inflation is still too high and a cut cycle is more likely to start in late 2027, with any further hike most likely in February 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Updated RBA staff forecasts in the February 2027 SMP would change the path.
